risks.summary: A terminal state in one record is not a terminal state in the record that describes the same event.
risks.detail: NEX-023 closed this on the resolve path: InvokeTool commits its ToolInvocation as `started` before entering the handler (correct - a crash must leave a trace), and ResolveInterruptedStep had settled the run without closing that row. NEX-024 found the same defect on the other settle path: AbortAgentRun flipped the run to aborted and never sealed the link, while AgentRun.abort also left a `started` step inside a terminal run. Both halves now settle, in one transaction. General rule, now proven to recur once: any operation that makes a run terminal must settle its mid-flight steps AND seal their invocations in the same transaction. A third settle path reopens this. Two records that disagree are not a partial success.
risks.status: closed on both existing settle paths (resolve: NEX-023; abort: NEX-024)

risks.summary: A field can be persisted, foreign-keyed, and written on every create — and still never be read by the check that needs it.
risks.detail: NEX-022: agent_runs.delegation_id was written by PlanAgentRun on every plan, carried a FK to agent_delegations, and was never consulted by AdvanceAgentRun._load_for_agent, which compared only agent_id. So a token from a different delegation could drive a run, and revoking the planning delegation did not stop it. The schema asserted the binding mattered; the read path disagreed, and nothing failed. General rule: for every security-relevant column, grep for the reads, not just the writes. A column written and never read is either dead or a missing check — decide which, in writing.

risks.summary: A control enforced on every path someone thought of can still miss a path that establishes the same identity.
risks.detail: NEX-006 closed the offboarding gap by calling ensure_tenant_access on the three human identity paths (OIDC callback, session resolution, bearer provider). Agent-token resolution was a fourth way to establish an identity and never called it, so a suspended delegator's agent stayed fully operational for as long as its token lived. The gap survived because the shared seam looked complete: every caller of ensure_tenant_access was correct, and nothing enumerated the callers that were missing. Lesson: when a check is 'the one place', list every identity-establishing path and assert each one calls it, rather than trusting the seam's existence. Closed for agent tokens by 990557d.

risks.summary: A governance gate can be structurally unusable while every test stays green.
risks.detail: NEX-016: human approval was implemented end to end (requests, decisions, expiry, revocation, HTTP routes, 8 tests) yet a durable run could never honour an approval. Two independent defects each alone made resumption impossible: the run failed terminally on the pause, and the unique (agent_id, idempotency_key) constraint was permanently consumed by the denial record. No test covered 'approve, then continue', so the suite was green through a decorative control. The general lesson: a security control needs a test of the full decision-to-effect path, not tests of each half.

risks.summary: A governance record can be unreachable through the API without any error, while the data is intact in storage.
risks.detail: NEX-015: approvals were persisted correctly and list_for_agent existed on the port, but the use case only ever called list_pending_for_agent, so every decided approval was invisible to its owner. No test failed and no exception was raised, because nothing asserted that a decision remained readable. The class is general: for each state a record can enter, check that some read path returns it. Closed for approvals by 414a222.

risks.summary: A slice can pass its tests and CI while the adapter that stores its invariant drops the field the check reads.
risks.detail: NEX-013 was VERIFIED on green CI while ApprovalRequestRepository.add() omitted expires_at, so the bound was inert for every gateway-created approval. The test used save(), which does write the columns. Pin security-relevant fields through the write path production uses. Closed for NEX-013 by 12584a1.

risks.summary: GitHub per-file diff stats truncate silently on a large PR.
risks.detail: On a diff over 20,000 lines, /pulls/{n}/files reports additions:0 for 20 files (every test file) and /pulls/{n}/diff returns HTTP 406, with no error on the stats endpoints to signal the truncation. Per-file sums gave 20,309 and /compare gave 19,366 against a true 27,659. Quote the PR object's additions field or `git diff --shortstat origin/main...HEAD` on a full clone.

risks.title: Coordinator CI notes go stale silently and read as current forever
risks.detail: Three claims in this repo's own docs were false at run start. STATE.md called ca15eb1 'docs-only and unclaimed' when it was 4/4 completed/success at that exact SHA. STATE.md carried PR counters of 28,385 additions / 88 commits when the PR object said 28,409 / 89. BACKLOG.md said 'CI has not yet run on c18bac7' when c18bac7 was 4/4 green. Each was written once at push time and never revisited. A note phrased 'CI has not yet run on X' has no expiry and is indistinguishable, to a later reader, from 'CI failed on X'. Mitigation: name the poll timestamp in any such note, and re-poll any not-yet-observed claim in the next run where that commit is reachable. Polling costs seconds.

risks.summary: A verifier that only checks a seal when the seal exists can be defeated by deleting the seal.
risks.detail: NEX-012 sealed each invocation's verdict in outcome_hash and NEX-012's tests proved that editing the verdict without touching the seal is caught. But verify_chain recomputed the seal only when one was present, so nulling outcome_hash and completed_at together removed the evidence instead of contradicting it, and the chain verified clean. The test attacked the weaker forgery. General rule: for every field a check reads, ask what the check does when that field is absent, and treat absence as a break wherever the state machine says the field must be present. Closed by NEX-018.
